To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the microstructure, pitting corrosion, stress corrosion cracking, and mechanical characteristics are affected by the input heat in welding processes.
the heat input of welding processes has significant effects on the microstructure and mechanical properties of DSS.
the effects of heat input on the microstructure of the welded DSS are different from those of ASS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of heat input on the corrosion and mechanical characteristics of the weldments of DUS.
the effects of heat input on the microstructure and properties of DSS weldments.
the effects of input heat in welding processes on the characteristics of DSS and ASS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
low-heat input welding is not always beneficial for DSS.
a high heat input in welding is beneficial to DSS, but not ASS.
the heat input should be increased to improve the microstructural homogeneity, mechanical properties, and corrosion resistance of the welded DSS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heat energy input in the welding process is an important factor that influences the microstructure, pitting corrosion, and mechanical properties in weldments of D.S.S.
the heat input in the welding process should be carefully considered for DSS.
the heat input in the welding process has an important influence on the microstructure and properties of the weldment of DSS.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, when welding DSS, the heat energy input should not be low to avoid the formation of ferrite in the weld zone, and the heat energy input is not too high to avoid the formation and growth of austenite in the HAZ.

the effects of heat input in welding process are more significant for the microstructure, pitting corrosion, mechanical properties, and stress-corrosion cracking (SCC) resistance of weldments of austenitic stainless steel.

a higher heat input can improve the mechanical properties and pitting corrosion resistance of DSS, but it can increase the susceptibility of DSS to intergranular stress cracking and stresscorrosion cracks.
